target_customer: Oncologists and breast cancer centers that choose and monitor neoadjuvant therapy; currently research institutions and hospitals under investigational use
problem: Patients can endure months of ineffective chemotherapy before response is known. NearWave makes a handheld near infrared imager to show early whether a therapy is working.
business_model: Medical device sales to hospitals and researchers (pre-commercial, investigational use only)
product_category: Handheld fdNIRS medical imaging device with iOS app

founders.name: Roy Stillwell
education: PhD in electrical engineering, biophotonics (University of Notre Dame graduate student per Notre Dame news)
founders.background_notes: YC page and Notre Dame news; originally from Colorado per YC page.

founders.name: Thomas O'Sullivan
prior_employers: University of Notre Dame (electrical engineering professor)
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC page and Notre Dame news; the idea started in a class he taught.

investors: University of Notre Dame McCloskey New Venture Competition (Grand Prize, Marshall County Prize, IrishAngels Award)

competitors.name: Boston University Roblyer group wearable diffuse optical probe
competitors.what: Academic wearable continuous wave probe for tumor hemodynamics during chemotherapy infusions
competitors.traction_then: Research prototype, not a commercial product

technical_complexity.rationale: A battery powered frequency domain NIRS device with quantitative tissue mapping needs custom optics, electronics and clinical validation, and it is regulated as a medical device.

defensibility.rationale: A university derived hardware design with a patent application (Nearwave Corp. applicant per search results) and regulatory hurdles; only academic rivals were found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found; no commercial diffuse optical breast monitoring startups appeared in my search.

market_need_then: Breast cancer therapy response is uncertain for months; academic papers dating to 2007 showed diffuse optical spectroscopy can predict response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

branding.domain_note: Uses nearwave.co, not a .com; no history found.

identity.logo: A NearWave wordmark in the site header
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and technical: tagline The Future Is Near Infrared, short feature phrases such as Non-Invasive. Non-Ionizing. Deep Tissue.

branding.brand_signature: The Future Is Near Infrared tagline
branding.community_and_virality: Notre Dame news coverage of prizes and a Techpoint 2021 Innovation of the Year Mira Award; no consumer community.

brand_strength.rationale: Name plays on near infrared and waves, but there is little brand press beyond university and regional award coverage and it resembles NextWave and similar names.

outcome_analysis: NearWave grew out of a Notre Dame class and won $100K in university competition prizes in April 2020 before joining YC in Winter 2022. The device is still investigational as of its site, with a team of three, and no priced equity round, exit or shutdown was found. It is a slow medical device path where regulatory clearance and clinical evidence, not software growth, set the pace.
notes: Sources disagree on founding year (2020 per YC bio and Notre Dame, 2021 and 2022 elsewhere). A VC database lists a July 2024 non-equity assistance entry without amount and the CEO profile says millions raised; both unverified and not recorded as rounds. The only competitors found are academic groups, with a 2017 source; no commercial rivals dated near the batch were found. Notre Dame Idea Center page returned 404. Austin location per YC page; South Bend per other profiles.
